capability_findings.observed: APB3-class signal set only. apb_spi_master exposes exactly the APB3 subset (apb_spi_master.sv:21-28) and spi_master_apb_if (spi_master_apb_if.sv:33-40) has the same ports; no PSTRB/PPROT/PWAKEUP/PUSER/PWUSER/PRUSER/PZERO appears anywhere in either file.

Register writes occur only for PSEL && PENABLE && PWRITE and each case arm writes a whole field from PWDATA; the TX-FIFO push takes all 32 bits of PWDATA. There is no byte-enable input, so a partial write cannot be expressed and would have to be a full-word write.
Hardwired constant: `assign PREADY = 1'b1;` - no wait states are possible; FIFO full cannot stall an APB access.

Hardwired constant: `assign PSLVERR = 1'b0;` - no APB error response is ever generated; a write to an undefined offset is silently dropped and a read of an undefined offset returns 0 via the read-mux default.

write_address and read_address are both PADDR[5:2], i.e. 16 word slots in a 64-byte window; the register map is 0x00 STATUS, 0x04 CLKDIV, 0x08 SPICMD, 0x0C SPIADR, 0x10 SPILEN, 0x14 SPIDUM, 0x18 TXFIFO, 0x20 RXFIFO, 0x24 INTCFG, 0x28 INTSTA. APB_ADDR_WIDTH only sets the port width; higher address bits are ignored (aliasing).

The read mux is a case on read_address only and is not gated by PSEL/PENABLE (spi_master_apb_if.sv:183-213). PRDATA is therefore a pure function of PADDR[5:2] and can be non-zero outside a valid APB access phase; an adapter must only sample it while the transfer is active.

events_o[0] is a one-cycle pulse generated by the TX/RX threshold state machines (s_int_tx|s_int_rx); events_o[1] is a one-cycle end-of-transfer pulse from s_eot. REG_INTSTA (0x28) has NO read-mux case item, so reading it returns 0, while that same read asserts spi_int_rd_sta and resets the interrupt state machine to the active state. There is no readable per-source interrupt status word.

A write to 0x18 pushes PWDATA into the 32-bit TX FIFO (spi_data_tx_valid), and a read of 0x20 returns and pops the 32-bit RX FIFO (spi_data_rx_ready). Both FIFOs are BUFFER_DEPTH=10 deep and are the only data path to/from the SPI engine.

In the default single-line mode MOSI is spi_sdo0 (tx: data_int[31], MSB first) and MISO is spi_sdi1 (rx shifts in sdi1). spi_sdi0 is the MOSI-side loopback; sdi2/sdi3 and sdo1..3 are only used in the quad modes, where sdo0..3 drive data_int[28..31] and sdi0..3 are sampled together.

SCK is generated from HCLK by spi_master_clkgen: it toggles when the counter reaches clk_div (period 2*(clk_div+1) HCLK cycles), is reset/idle low and only stops while low when en=0; spi_rise is asserted on the 0->1 toggle and spi_fall on the 1->0 toggle. The controller shifts TX data on spi_fall (tx_edge) and samples RX data on spi_rise (rx_edge), i.e. CPOL=0/CPHA=0 (SPI mode 0): the leading edge is rising and is the sampling edge.

No CPOL/CPHA/polarity/phase register, port or signal exists in either PULP repo (case-insensitive search finds no match); the timing is hardwired to mode 0. The spi_mode output is the line-width mode, not polarity/phase: SPI_STD=2'b00, SPI_QUAD_TX=2'b01, SPI_QUAD_RX=2'b10.

spi_csn[i] = ~spi_csreg[i] | spi_cs; spi_cs is 0 for the whole transfer (IDLE only sets it 1), so all selected CS lines assert at transfer start and release together when the FSM returns to IDLE. spi_csreg is loaded from PWDATA[11:8] on a REG_STATUS write and is not decoded, so several CS lines can be asserted simultaneously and there is no per-frame or per-byte CS control.

spi_swrst (PWDATA[4] on a REG_STATUS write) only drives clr_i of the two FIFOs (apb_spi_master.sv:300 and :322). spi_master_controller declares spi_swrst but never references it (`//FIXME Not used at all`), so software reset does not reset the SPI FSM, bit counters or clock generator.

A transfer is: command bits from spi_cmd (spi_cmd_len), address bits from spi_addr (spi_addr_len), optional dummy bits (spi_dummy_rd for reads / spi_dummy_wr for writes), then data. spi_data_len is a BIT count (counter_tx/counter_rx are loaded with spi_data_len) and TX/RX assemble 32-bit words at counter[4:0]==31 boundaries.
Single HCLK domain with asynchronous active-low reset; SCK is generated logic (an output of the clkgen), not a clock input, and all SPI pins are in the HCLK domain.

Closure equals the apb_spi_master entry of the repo filelist: the two apb-spi files plus the five shared spi_master_* files pinned by pulp_spi_dependencies/axi-spi. Verilator elaborates 8 module instances with BUFFER_DEPTH=10/APB_ADDR_WIDTH=12, exit 0 with 10 warnings. Dropping any of the seven files fails (MODMISSING naming the exact instantiation site); re-running in a tree containing only those files reproduces exit 0 with the same warning count.

unsupported.reason: No PSTRB input and no per-byte write enable; all APB writes are full 32-bit words, so byte/partial register writes cannot be expressed.
No PPROT/PWAKEUP/PUSER/PWUSER/PRUSER ports and PSLVERR is tied 0, so no APB protection or error response can be driven or observed.
PREADY is tied to 1'b1, so the peripheral can never stall an APB access (e.g. when a FIFO is full the write is simply accepted/dropped by the FIFO logic with no backpressure).
SPI mode is hardwired to CPOL=0/CPHA=0; there is no polarity/phase register or port, so modes 1/2/3 cannot be configured or tested.
REG_INTSTA (0x28) reads return 0 because the read mux has no case item for it, even though the read acknowledges the interrupt pulse; there is no readable per-source interrupt status.
spi_swrst is not connected to the controller FSM: it only clears the FIFOs, so a software reset cannot abort or restart an in-flight transfer.
spi_csn[i] is driven directly from spi_csreg bits without decoding and is asserted for the entire transfer, so simultaneous CS assertion is possible and per-byte CS framing is impossible.
SCK is generated from HCLK and is not a clock input; an externally clocked SPI slave/master configuration is not supported by this RTL.
